title: A merge gate that fails closed
goal: Fix a naive gate script so it blocks a merge unless three gate statuses are green on the head commit, CI is green, the labels are present and the branch is current. Prove it against a seeded bad PR.
setup_cmd: mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-5-3-gates/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-5-3-gates && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-5-3-gates && git init -q -b main && git add -A && git -c user.name=fm-learner -c user.email=learner@example.com commit -q -m baseline && npm install

starter_prompts.claude: Read RULES.md, AGENTS.md and tests/gate.test.mjs. gate.mjs is naive on purpose. Run npm test, then fix gate.mjs so every rule in RULES.md holds. Never edit tests/ or fixtures/. Before you code, tell me in one sentence why a gate approval must be tied to the head SHA, and which fixture proves it.
starter_prompts.codex: Read RULES.md, AGENTS.md and tests/gate.test.mjs. gate.mjs is naive on purpose. Run npm test, then fix gate.mjs so every rule in RULES.md holds. Never edit tests/ or fixtures/. Before you code, tell me in one sentence why a gate approval must be tied to the head SHA, and which fixture proves it.

solution_notes: Statuses only count when they were posted on the head SHA, and the latest one per gate wins. This is the rule our own review caught in scripts/gate-status.sh: without it, an approval can silently cover a commit nobody reviewed.
An empty list of CI check runs blocks the merge. 'Nothing ran' looks identical to 'nothing failed' unless you check for it.
The gate collects every reason instead of stopping at the first, so the author fixes everything in one round trip.
Bad or missing input fails closed. evaluate({}) is blocked, and a missing behind_by is treated as unknown rather than zero.
